status: exact point-ensemble orientation observable and parametric reach map; finite-size material response and UV matching remain external

model.potential: V=f_e^2 sigma_1^i sigma_2^j partial_i partial_j exp(-m r)/(4 pi r)
model.pointEnsembleCondition: each polarized body is small compared with both the separation and the force-variation scale; otherwise use the displayed six-dimensional spin-density convolution

nullTests: the separated signal vanishes when either body is depolarized
the transverse torque vanishes at theta=0 and pi and is maximal at theta=pi/2
reversing either polarization reverses the signal
the radial/transverse ratio must obey rho>=2 and yield the same nonnegative mass at every separation

finiteSizeObservable.energy: U=f_e^2 integral d^3x d^3y s_1^i(x) s_2^j(y) partial_i partial_j Y_m(|x-y|)
finiteSizeObservable.interpretation: s_a^i is the species-weighted polarized electron number density; geometry, shielding and magnetic leakage enter the experimental forward model rather than the particle-level kernel
finiteSizeObservable.massExtraction: the analytic point ratio is replaced by the ratio of two geometry form factors, both computable from the same measured spin-density maps

reachFormula.naturalUnits: y_e,min=sqrt[16 pi m_e^2 r^3 tau_min exp(x)/(N_eff (x+1))]
reachFormula.meaning: tau_min is the resolved transverse torque amplitude expressed as an energy; r and m_e are in inverse common natural units
reachFormula.degeneracy: a force measurement determines m_phi and f_e, but A, B and c_e are not separately identifiable without UV or matter-sector matching

illustrativeDesignPoint.classification: sensitivity scaling example, not a claim about an existing apparatus or achievable magnetic systematics
illustrativeDesignPoint.interpretation: even this optimistic point-ensemble scaling probes a coupling many orders above the natural Planck-normalized benchmark; making the pole light while retaining weak coupling requires a very large B coefficient

decision: The phenomenology branch can be advanced without inventing finite Wilson coefficients: a dual-orientation polarized electron experiment first extracts the range from a coupling-free tensor ratio and then extracts f_e from the absolute torque. The remaining blocker is no longer the observable; it is material-specific finite-size modeling plus UV matching of c_e, A and B.
